title: BUDGET-LOMO: was leave-one-ANCHOR-out the wrong fold structure? (zero calls; BUDGET-TRANSFER's first reading suggested the leakage runs along the MODEL axis)
question: Leave-one-MODEL-out on the 891 x12 edges (for each of the 12 models remove every edge touching it, fit b0 and b1 on the remainder, score the held-out edges), beside leave-one-anchor-out (14) and leave-one-pair-out (66) on the identical edge set: does the calibration claim survive (LOMO of the same order as LOAO's 2.4x); the spread of b1 across folds; utility under LOMO.

review.verdict: the review upheld BUDGET-LOMO as a genuine self-falsification and required the McNemar column, the 'scored twice' correction and the withdrawal of the b1-swing explanation (batch 4 of the corrections, d4eec8d)

criteria.text: PRIMARY: the realised wrong-direction rate among LOMO-held-out called edges against its nominal; the calibration claim survives only if LOMO is of the same order as LOAO's 2.4x
criteria.value: with McNemar-established counts: in sample 665 / 2(1) / 1.30 = 1.5x; raw certificate 739 / 8(4) / 0.83 = 9.7x (empirical set, Gaussian nominal; consistent alternatives 9.3x / 10.5x); LOAO 663 / 3(2) / 1.27 = 2.4x; LOPO 664 / 3(2) / 1.29 = 2.3x; LOMO last-fold-wins 666 / 3(2) / 1.18 = 2.5x (1.7x established); LOMO first-fold-wins 668 / 3(2) / 1.30 = 2.3x: the same order; the claim STANDS

criteria.text: the spread of b1 across the 12 LOMO folds
criteria.value: b1 swings 2.61x, +2.0529 (withhold iask_pro) to +5.3673 (withhold deepseek-v2.5); CORRECTED: b0 and b1 co-vary at about -0.99 across folds, so the swing in b1 alone overstates tau's swing at mid agreement and understates it at low agreement; neither 'unstable parameter' nor 'stable despite it' is established by the table

predictions.text: LOMO comes in materially worse than LOAO (4x to 8x) and the anchor fold exposed as an artefact
predictions.value: 2.3-2.5x: the model-axis fold is indistinguishable from the anchor fold, so the anchor fold was not hiding model-axis leakage and the adopted figure stands

predictions.text: b1 swings by more than a factor of two across folds
predictions.value: 2.61x; but the 'b1 swings while calibration is stable' explanation is withdrawn (b0 / b1 co-vary at -0.99)

falsifier.text: for the budget itself: if LOMO exceeds the raw certificate's own 9.7x, the widener adds nothing and should be withdrawn in favour of the agreement gate
falsifier.note: does not fire (2.5x vs 9.7x); against the parameter-free gate on the same edges the budget gives 666 called / 3 wrong / 68 correct surrendered against A < 0.65's 608 / 3 / 126: at matched error it surrenders half as many correct calls, out of fold and along the model axis

numbers_of_record.review_fixes: (a) McNemar-established counts added (LOMO 1.7x established; LOAO / LOPO the same 2 events); (b) the 'scored twice' note was wrong (one score per edge; both conventions printed, agree within 0.2x); (c) the b1-swing explanation withdrawn

sentence_of_record: BUDGET-LOMO, CORRECTED (2026-09-15, zero calls): the conclusion stands and now carries what it lacked: with McNemar-established counts LOAO 663/3(2)/1.27 = 2.4x, LOPO 664/3(2)/1.29 = 2.3x, LOMO 666/3(2)/1.18 = 2.5x all, 1.7x established (first-fold-wins 668/3(2)/1.30 = 2.3x); the model-axis fold is indistinguishable from the anchor fold, so the anchor fold was not hiding model-axis leakage and the adopted 2.4x figure stands; the prediction (4-8x) FAILED; the falsifier (LOMO worse than the raw certificate's 9.7x) does not fire; the 'b1 swings 2.6x while calibration is stable' explanation is withdrawn (b0 and b1 co-vary at -0.99), so neither instability nor robustness-to-it is shown by the b1 column; utility 74.4-74.7% throughout.

plain_description.what: Re-tests the calibration of the error-budget widener for the ranking certificate. Each fold leaves out every comparison involving one model (12 folds). This is set beside leaving out one subject area or one model pair, all on the same 891 comparison edges. No judge calls.
plain_description.why: An earlier reading suggested that leaving out one subject area might hide errors that run along models, which would make the adopted 2.4x calibration figure too optimistic.
plain_description.information: If leaving out a model gave much worse calibration, the adopted figure would be wrong. Result: done (corrected rerun). All three fold types agree: 2.3x to 2.5x overall, 1.7x on statistically established edges. So the adopted 2.4x stands, and the predicted 4-8x failed. The falsifier did not fire. One earlier explanation (about parameter instability) was withdrawn. It was judged on the arena pool later ruled 'history, not evidence'.
